nodes.name: When Called By Another Workflow
nodes.notes: The shared backend. Workflow 01 (Gmail) and workflow 02 (live chat) both call THIS workflow - not a copy of it - so a change to how the desk answers is one edit in one place, and the two channels can never drift apart. Input: { channel, text, session_or_thread_id, history[] }.

nodes.name: Normalise Request
nodes.notes: Validates the contract and builds the retrieval query. Splitting the quoted reply block off the bottom of an email is what keeps thread number three from retrieving the same articles as thread number one.

parameters.query:
-- Postgres full-text search over the business knowledge base.
--
-- The query is ORed, not ANDed. plainto_tsquery and websearch_to_tsquery both
-- join every word with &, which means one unusual word anywhere in a customer's
-- sentence excludes the article that answers them: "I was charged twice this
-- month, can I get a refund?" ANDs charged & twice & month & refund and matches
-- nothing at all. Swapping & for | turns it into what a search box does - match
-- anything, then rank - and the ranking plus the floor in the next node are what
-- keep the noise out.
--
-- Built by rewriting plainto_tsquery's OUTPUT rather than by assembling a
-- tsquery from the raw string: plainto_tsquery has already stemmed the words and
-- discarded every operator character, so nothing a customer can type reaches
-- to_tsquery as syntax.
--
-- ts_rank reads the weights set on articles.search_tsv, so a title match beats a
-- passing mention in a body. The floor that decides "no match at all" is applied
-- in the next node, not here, because it has to be visible in the execution.
WITH q AS (
  SELECT nullif(replace(plainto_tsquery('english', $1)::text, '&', '|'), '')::tsquery AS tsq
)
SELECT a.id,
       a.slug,
       a.title,
       a.category,
       left(a.body, 1500) AS passage,
       round(ts_rank(a.search_tsv, q.tsq)::numeric, 6) AS relevance
  FROM articles a, q
 WHERE q.tsq IS NOT NULL
   AND a.search_tsv @@ q.tsq
 ORDER BY relevance DESC, a.updated_at DESC
 LIMIT $2::int;

nodes.name: Retrieve Passages
nodes.notes: Real retrieval against a real index - no vector database, and honest about being lexical. A question with no lexical overlap with any article returns zero rows, which is the missing-knowledge case the brief asks for, arriving as data rather than as an error.

nodes.name: Apply Relevance Floor
nodes.notes: The floor is what turns a bad retrieval into an honest "I do not know" instead of a confident wrong answer built out of a loosely related article.

nodes.name: Anything Retrieved?
nodes.notes: True: there is at least one passage above the floor to answer from. False: the knowledge base has nothing on this, which is a documented outcome, not a failure.

nodes.name: Answer From Passages
nodes.notes: The model sees the retrieved passages and nothing else - no store of its own, no browsing, no earlier context beyond the history turns. That is what "grounded" means here, and it is enforced again in Validate Answer, because a prompt is a request and not a guarantee.

nodes.name: Validate Answer
nodes.notes: Parses the response, drops any citation the model invented, and derives the confidence the gate upstream reads. A model that claims it answered but cites nothing is not grounded here.

nodes.name: Answered From The Knowledge Base?
nodes.notes: The missing-knowledge branch. False means retrieval found articles but none of them contained the answer - a different gap from "nothing matched at all", and both are recorded with their own reason.

nodes.name: Result: Not Answerable From The Knowledge Base
Ungrounded Result
nodes.notes: A junction, not a transform. The three ungrounded branches meet here so the unanswered-questions write and the return contract are each defined in exactly one place.

parameters.query:
-- The knowledge base's own to-do list.
--
-- ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, not DO NOTHING: the same question asked fifty times
-- must be one row with asked_count = 50, not fifty rows nobody reads. The
-- counter is the whole value of the table - it says which article to write next.
--
-- The WHERE clause keeps an outage out of the gap list. A model that was down is
-- not a question the help centre failed to answer, and mixing the two would make
-- the list untrustworthy on the one day it matters.
INSERT INTO unanswered_questions (question_hash, question, channel, conversation_ref, reason)
SELECT $1, $2, $3, $4, $5
 WHERE $5 IN ('no_matching_article', 'not_answerable_from_kb')
    ON CONFLICT (question_hash) DO UPDATE
   SET asked_count   = unanswered_questions.asked_count + 1,
       last_asked_at = now()
RETURNING id, asked_count;

nodes.name: Record Unanswered Question
nodes.notes: Writes nothing when the reason was an outage, which is why alwaysOutputData is on: the branch must keep moving even when the INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE inserts no row.

nodes.name: Return To Caller
nodes.notes: Returns { grounded, answer, confidence, used_article_ids, escalate_reason, ... }. Workflows 01 and 02 both gate on exactly these fields.
